rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first creation is a greater precedent than resurrection: the One who created humans from nothing can recreate them after they perish.
rows.anchor: وهو الخلق الأول . قال تعالى : { أفعيينا بالخلق الأول بل هم في لبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address principally targets polytheists, since they denied resurrection; their inclusion here is clearer than in the preceding address.
rows.anchor: ودخول المشركين بادىء ذي بدء في هذا الخطاب أظهر من دخولهم في الخطاب السابق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported view takes the address here as specifically directed to the polytheists.
rows.anchor: قيل إن الخطاب هنا خاص بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional presents their actual doubt as though it were uncertain, given the surrounding proofs that should dispel it.
rows.anchor: وجعل ريبهم في البعث مفروضا ب ( إن ) الشرطية مع أن ريبهم محقق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction resembles the conditional in 43:5, where a condition is posed despite its factual premise.
rows.anchor: أفنضرب عنكم الذكر صفحا أن كنتم قوما مسرفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition in ‘in doubt’ is figurative: doubt is portrayed as enclosing those who experience it.
rows.anchor: شبهت ملابسة الريب إياهم بإحاطة الظرف بالمظروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation clause occupies the answer’s position but is evidence for the answer, not its literal wording; the implied response is to know or consider resurrection possible.
rows.anchor: واقعة موقع جواب الشرط ولكنها لا يصلح لفظها لأن يكون جوابا لهذا الشرط بل هي دليل الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first human origin from dust is Adam and Eve; reproductive capacity was then established in Adam and his spouse, so later generation is from semen.
rows.anchor: وهو آدم عليه السلام وحواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṭfa means a man’s semen and is a noun on the pattern fuʿla with the passive sense ‘that which is poured’; the root denotes drops or pouring.
rows.anchor: اسم لمني الرجل ، وهو بوزن فعلة بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlaqa is a soft, clotted piece of blood.
rows.anchor: القطعة من الدم الجامد اللين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḍgha is a piece of flesh about the size of a morsel to chew; its form conveys something chewed or of chewed size.
rows.anchor: القطعة من اللحم بقدر ما يمضغ مثله ،

words: ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here thumma coordinates individual developmental stages and marks genuine temporal succession.
rows.anchor: عاطفة مفردات فهي للتراخي الحقيقي

words: فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every fetus has a divinely determined term in the womb, usually nine months and nine days, though an intervening cause may bring delivery sooner; all is known to God.
rows.anchor: الأكثر استكمال تسعة أشهر وتسعة أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He connects the phrase ‘appointed term’ with the same wording in the debt verse, 2:282.
rows.anchor: إلى أجل مسمى فاكتبوه في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks rank or importance here, because the fetus’s emergence is the point at issue.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على التراخي الرتبي فإن إخراج الجنين هو المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭiflan is a circumstantial accusative describing the addressees as infants; its singular form denotes the generic class and functions like a plural.
rows.anchor: أي حال كونكم أطفالا . وإنما أفرد { طفلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘then that you reach maturity’ is linked to bringing infants out as its cause, with the lām expressing purpose.
rows.anchor: والمعلل فعل { نخرجكم طفلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Full strength is the complete wisdom behind human development: it is the body’s and mind’s strongest, clearest display of human capacities.
rows.anchor: وإنما جعل بلوغ الأشد علة لأنه أقوى أطوار الإنسان وأجلى مظاهر مواهبه في الجسم والعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second thumma reinforces the earlier thumma in the sequence about being brought out as infants.
rows.anchor: تأكيد لمثله في قوله { ثم نخرجكم طفلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He presents his account of how this clause connects to its context and says the commentators’ alternative explanations, cited by al-Alusi, do not withstand scrutiny.
rows.anchor: هذا ما ظهر لي في اتصال هذه الجملة بما قبلها وللمفسرين توجيهات غير سالمة من التعقب ذكرها الألوسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd means the age of youth, when one’s powers are fully gathered.
rows.anchor: والأشد : سن الفتوة واستجماع القوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He points to Joseph receiving judgment and knowledge upon reaching full strength in 12:22.
rows.anchor: ولما بلغ أشده آتيناه حكما وعلما

words: أَشُدَّكُمْ وَمِنكُم مَّن يُتَوَفَّىٰ وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike 40:67, this proof omits old age because it emphasizes growth toward strength, not decline; 40:67 mentions old age as a life stage people desire, while this address warns that some will reach senility.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر في آية سورة الحج لأنها وردت مورد الاستدلال على الإحياء بعد العدم فلم يذكر فيها من الأطوار إلا ما فيه ازدياد القوة ونماء الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth’s revival argument is coordinated with the earlier creation argument and addressed generally to anyone hearing the discourse.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة { فإنا خلقناكم من تراب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This advances the proof by analogy from a visible event; the initial creation argument began with an unseen origin, whereas the earth’s revival can be observed.
rows.anchor: وهذا ارتقاء في الاستدلال على الإحياء بعد الموت بقياس التمثيل لأنه استدلال بحالة مشاهدة

words: فَإِذَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَآءَ ٱهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof lies especially in water making the earth rise and grow: its barrenness images death, and its renewed growth images resurrection.
rows.anchor: فهمود الأرض بمنزلة موت الإنسان واهتزازها وإنباتها بعد ذلك يماثل الإحياء بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamida describes dry earth with its vegetation gone; for fire, the related word means extinguished.
rows.anchor: فهمود الأرض جفافها وزوال نبتها ، وهمود النار خمودها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihtazz means movement upward; the earth is pictured as rising under rain and as its surface rises with grass, like something shaking upward.
rows.anchor: التحرك إلى أعلى ، فاهتزاز الأرض تمثيل لحال ارتفاع ترابها بالماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabat means increased or swollen; here the land swells as plants and trees emerge through it.
rows.anchor: وهو ازدياد الشيء يقال : ربا يربو ربوا ، وفسر هنا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads rabāʾat with hamza after the bāʾ, meaning that the earth rose.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر { وربأت بهمزة مفتوحة بعد الموحدة ، أي ارتفعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamzated reading is supported by ‘to rise above’ in rabāʾa binafsihi and by the lookout called rabīʾa, who stands on a hill to watch for enemies.
rows.anchor: ربأ بنفسه عن كذا ، أي ارتفع مجازا ، وهو فعل مشتق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawj first denotes a paired male or female kind, then came to denote either kind individually and, more broadly, any type or species, as here for plants.
rows.anchor: أطلق عليه اسم الزوج تشبيها له بالزوج من الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bahīj means pleasing to look at; the description embeds a grace for humanity, since beauty contributes no proof of resurrection.
rows.anchor: والبهيج : الحسن المنظر السار للناظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gratuitous mention of pleasing appearance parallels blessings in 16:6 and the adornment of the lowest heaven in 67:5.
rows.anchor: ولكم فيها جمال حين تريحون وحين تسرحون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement is a concluding summary and tailpiece referring to human creation, development and death, and the earth’s revival and vegetation.
rows.anchor: فذلكة لما تقدم ، فالجملة تذييل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular address attached to the demonstrative is generic, following the address in ‘you see the earth barren’; singular address is also the construction’s basic form.
rows.anchor: لإرادة مخاطب غير معين على نسق قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ may express cause, but he prefers accompaniment: creation and growth occur alongside the truth of God’s divinity, as evidence is bound to what it proves; this is more elegant and comprehensive.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الباء للملابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥaqq means the established, indisputable reality; the restriction means God alone, unlike the nonexistent idols people worship.
rows.anchor: والحق : الثابت الذي لا مراء فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He supports the claim that idols are merely names with the statement in 22:23 that they are names made up by people without divine authority.
rows.anchor: إن هي إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing God alone as real is the root proof because shirk underlies the other errors of its adherents.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاستدلال هو أصل بقية الأدلة لأنه نقض للشرك الذي هو الأصل لجميع ضلالات أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining assertions after God is the Real explain how resurrection is possible, supported by causal evidence for God’s existence and power and analogical evidence for resurrection and the Hour.
rows.anchor: فهي لبيان إمكان البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five stated matters follow from human and earthly development: effects point to God and His power, while analogies show resurrection, the Hour and raising from graves are possible.
rows.anchor: أن تلك الأحوال دالة على هذه الأمور الخمسة : إما بدلالة المسبب على السبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once the possibility of resurrection is established, its occurrence should be believed: the deniers’ only barrier was assuming it impossible, though recreating what was first created from nothing is more readily possible.
rows.anchor: وإذا تبين إمكان ذلك حق التصديق بوقوعه لأنهم لم يكن بينهم وبين التصديق به حائل إلا ظنهم استحالته

words: إِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍۢ مِنَ ٱلْبَعْثِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The new disputants passage continues the address about doubt: after the proofs, people divide into those convinced and those who still dispute without knowledge.
rows.anchor: فالناس بعد ذلك فريقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘there is no doubt in it’ interrupts the coordinated clauses and denies the genus of doubt, meaning doubt is simply absent.
rows.anchor: وجملة { لا ريب فيها } ( الحج : 7 ) معترضة بين المتعاطفات

words: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَٰدِلُ فِى ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies this disputing group with the group in 22:3, who follow every rebellious devil; here they argue after hearing the warning and seeing the resurrection proofs.
rows.anchor: والمعني بهذه الآية هو المعني بقوله فيما مضى

words: بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍۢ وَلَا هُدًۭى وَلَا كِتَٰبٍۢ مُّنِيرٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their first dispute, after a warning of the Hour, stems from ignorance and satanic whispering; after proofs, they know the subject but lack guidance or revealed law, reject the proof arrogantly and seek to mislead others.
rows.anchor: ودافعهم إلى الجدال في الله عند وضوح الأدلة على البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The different motives belong to one group, the people of shirk and misguidance, whose prominent leaders include al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, Abū Jahl and Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: فيؤول إلى معنى أن أحوال هؤلاء مختلفة وأصحابها فريق واحد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported identification takes the disputant in this verse to be al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, with the repetition clarifying his two modes of disputation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد من هذه الآية بمن يجادل في الله : النضر بن الحارث

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported identification names Abū Jahl as the disputant here.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بمن يجادل في هذه الآية أبو جهل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view assigns al-Naḍr to the preceding verse and Abū Jahl to this one, treating each verse as restricted by its occasion of revelation.
rows.anchor: كما قيل : إن المراد في الآية الماضية النضر بن الحارث فجعلت الآية خاصة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited for the view that this disputant verse is restricted to a particular occasion of revelation.
rows.anchor: وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported identification is al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو الأخنس بن شريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He distinguishes the earlier group as the polytheists’ followers who imitate their chiefs, and this verse’s group as the leaders of unbelief themselves.
rows.anchor: المقلدون بكسر اللام من المشركين الذين يتبعون ما تمليه عليهم سادة الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says those disputing here without guidance are the leaders of unbelief, whose followers imitate them.
rows.anchor: المقلدون بفتح اللام أئمة الكفر

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This begins a fresh proof that God alone is divine and answers the call to other beings in 22:12–13, whose helplessness was just described.
rows.anchor: جملة مستأنفة لابتداء استدلال على انفراد الله تعالى بالإلهية

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The material between these linked passages is a digression and parenthetical insertion.
rows.anchor: وما وقع بين هاتين الجملتين استطراد واعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeing is intellectual rather than visual, the address is generic, and the interrogative reproaches listeners for failing to know what creation’s states prove.
rows.anchor: علمية . والخطاب لغير معين . والاستفهام إنكاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the address may be to the Prophet as a confirmatory question, since his knowledge of this point is established in al-Raʿd and al-Naḥl.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الخطاب للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم والاستفهام تقريريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes prostration here in both its literal and figurative senses, rejecting al-Zamakhsharī’s objection.
rows.anchor: وقد استعمل السجود في حقيقته ومجازه ، وهو حسن وإن أباه الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For nonhuman beings, prostration is figurative: their created state shows that they are subject to God’s ordering and command.
rows.anchor: أن سجود الموجودات غير الإنسانية ليس إلا دلالة تلك الموجودات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many humans do literally prostrate to God, but many others turn from such worship or prostrate to idols; this visible conduct obscures the figurative sign of their created dependence.
rows.anchor: فلما خالطها إعراض كثير من الناس عن السجود لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Many are liable to punishment’ alludes to their abandoning worship of God; the polytheists deserve the fire by God’s decree and warning.
rows.anchor: عن ترك السجود لله ، أي حق عليهم العذاب

words: وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whom God humiliates through their liability to punishment have no one to honor them with victory or intercession.
rows.anchor: أن الله أهانهم باستحقاق العذاب فلا يجدون من يكرمهم بالنصر أو بالشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause supplies the cause for both parenthetical statements; its emphatic inna conveys concern and thus takes on a causal force.
rows.anchor: وجود حرف التوكيد في أول الجملة مع عدم المنكر يمحض حرف التوكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists unanimously count this passage as a place for prostration of recitation.
rows.anchor: وهذا موضع سجود من سجود القرآن باتفاق الفقهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next passage is a connected descent and a clarifying answer to the question raised by the punished group in 22:18: what is the punishment they face?
rows.anchor: مقتضى سياق السورة واتصال آي السورة وتتابعها في النزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual demonstrative points to the two sides implied in 22:18: people of monotheism who worship God and polytheists who worship others.
rows.anchor: فاسم الإشارة المثنى مشير إلى ما يفيده قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is appositional to ‘those who fight’ in 22:39; it shows that their fighting began as persecution, whose gravest form was expulsion.
rows.anchor: بدل من { الذين يقاتلون } ( الحج : 39 ) ، وفي إجراء هذه الصلة عليهم إيماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-ghayri ḥaqq is circumstantial: the expelled people were in a state of having no valid ground on which expulsion could be imposed.
rows.anchor: أي أخرجوا متلبسين بعدم الحق عليهم الموجب إخراجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People have a natural right to remain in their homeland and among their people, on equal terms with the established community, whether rooted in long settlement or conquest.
rows.anchor: فإن للمرء حقا في وطنه ومعاشرة قومه ، وهذا الحق ثابت بالفطرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That right ends only under a basis set by religious law or established pre-religious custom; legal exile and banishment and pre-Islamic expulsion were penalties for wrongdoing when lesser restraint failed.
rows.anchor: ولا يزول ذلك الحق إلا بموجب قرره الشرع أو العوائد قبل الشرع

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr’s verse lists an oath, a contest or departure as the three ways a right may be brought to an end.
rows.anchor: كما قال زهير : فإن الحق مقطعه ثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith in God entails no aggression against others, and merely declaring it harms no one; expulsion for that reason is blatant injustice enforced by force.
rows.anchor: فإن إيمانهم بالله لا ينجر منه اعتداء على غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception ironically treats professing God as the sole supposed ground for expulsion, thereby reinforcing that no real ground exists; it praises by seeming to blame.
rows.anchor: وهذا من تأكيد الشيء بما يوهم نقضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is rhetorically drawn from the general idea of a valid ground, while the intended ground is one that would justify expelling them; its ironic force surveys and dismisses any imagined justification.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء في قوله : { إلا أن يقولوا ربنا الله } استثناء من عموم الحق

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha’s couplet illustrates praise framed to resemble blame: the only supposed flaw is that swords have battle nicks.
rows.anchor: ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was certainly revealed in Medina.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية لا محالة نزلت بالمدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This parenthesis explains and honors the permission to defend in 22:39; that defense protects the worship of Muslims, Jews and Christians, benefiting all monotheists rather than Muslims alone.
rows.anchor: فلما تضمنت جملة { أذن للذين يقاتلون } ( الحج : 39 ) الخ الإذن للمسلمين بدفاع المشركين عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw introduces a parenthetical, resumptive clause that explains the content of the permission to fight in 22:39.
rows.anchor: والواو في قوله { ولولا دفاع الله الناس } إلى آخره ، اعتراضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawlā is a counterfactual conditional: its consequent is withheld because the condition stated in its clause exists.
rows.anchor: حرف امتناع لوجود ، أي حرف يدل على امتناع جوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without defense of Muslim worship places, polytheists would have overcome the Muslims, attacked neighboring non-polytheist communities and destroyed their temples to erase monotheism; naming other temples also urges support for Muslims.
rows.anchor: ولهدموا معابدهم من صوامع ، وبيعع ، وصلوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this interpretation, al-nās is context-specific: the people fighting one another are the Muslims and Meccan polytheists.
rows.anchor: فالتعريف في { الناس } تعريف العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also allows a general historical reading: before Islam, God permitted earlier monotheists to fight, as in David’s victory over Goliath and Solomon’s rule, to prevent polytheists from erasing signs of monotheism as Nebuchadnezzar erased Solomon’s temple.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد : لولا ما سبق قبل الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that alternative, al-nās is generic and the clause concludes the permission in 22:39: earlier permission to fight kept polytheists from oppressing monotheists as they had done before.
rows.anchor: فتكون هذه الجملة تذييلا لجملة { أذن للذين يقاتلون بأنهم ظلموا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing the defense directly to God is a figurative causal attribution: His permission caused people to defend their temples, urging religious communities to unite against polytheism.
rows.anchor: وإضافة الدفاع إلى الله إسناد مجازي عقلي

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Abū Jaʿfar and Yaʿqūb read difāʿ, with an alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع ، وأبو جعفر ، ويعقوب { دفاع . }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿḍahum is a partitive apposition to al-nās, and bi-baʿḍin attaches to difāʿ with bāʾ of instrument.
rows.anchor: بدل من { الناس } بدل بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadm means demolishing a structure and bringing it down.
rows.anchor: والهدم : تقويض البناء وتسقيطه

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū Jaʿfar read the verb with a light dāl; the other readers double it to intensify the destruction, as if rage left no trace.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع ، وابن كثير ، وأبو جعفر { لهدمت } بتخفيف الدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣawāmiʿ are tall, narrow buildings reached by stairs, with an upper chamber used by monks for secluded worship; lamps aided night prayer and travelers, hence the related name manāra.
rows.anchor: والصوامع : جمع صومعة بوزن فوعلة

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s image of a monk’s lantern-like tower at evening illustrates the meaning of manāra.
rows.anchor: تضيء الظلام بالعشي كأنها منارة ممسى راهب متبتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biyaʿ are Christian places of worship; the word’s etymology is unknown and may be borrowed from another language.
rows.anchor: والبيع : جمع بيعة بكسر الباء وسكون التحتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣalawāt here means Jewish synagogues, borrowed from Syriac ṣlōthā and adapted into Arabic.
rows.anchor: والصلوات : جمع صلاة وهي هنا مراد بها كنائس اليهود

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid, al-Jaḥdarī, Abū al-ʿĀliya and Abū Rajāʾ are reported to read the word with a final thāʾ.
rows.anchor: أنهم قرأوها هنا { وصلواث } بمثلثة في آخره

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports that ʿIkrima and Mujāhid read ṣalwaythā with the stated vowel pattern and a shortened alif.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : قرأ عكرمة ، ومجاهد { صلويثا بكسر الصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He remarks that the lexicographers’ failure to record this word or material is astonishing.
rows.anchor: وهذه المادة قد فاتت أهل اللغة وهي غفلة عجيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masājid here denotes places of prostration not among the three preceding kinds of worship buildings; the passage applies as Muslims build the mosques of Qubāʾ and Medina at the start of the Hijra.
rows.anchor: والمساجد : اسم لمحل السجود من كل موضع عبادة
